text: Under no circumstances should the ancient scrolls be removed from the library.
tip: Stress NO CIR-cum-stan-ces. 'ancient' is /ˈeɪnʃənt/. Keep /skr/ together in 'scrolls'.

text: Scarcely had the dragon closed its eyes when a faint rustling stirred the shadows.
tip: The t in 'rustling' is silent: /ˈrʌslɪŋ/. Stress SCARCE-ly.

text: Her argument, though ostensibly watertight, rests on a rather tenuous assumption.
tip: os-TEN-si-bly, TEN-u-ous /ˈtenjuəs/, as-SUMP-tion. Lower your pitch for the inserted clause.

text: It goes without saying that the committee will have to bite the bullet sooner or later.
tip: 'goes without saying' is one chunk. Stress BITE and BUL-let, and link 'sooner or later' with an r.

text: Much as I admire his tenacity, I can't condone the way he treated his rivals.
tip: te-NAC-i-ty /təˈnæsəti/ and con-DONE. Contrast ad-MIRE with CAN'T.

text: The historian's account, meticulously researched as it is, glosses over several inconvenient truths.
tip: me-TIC-u-lous-ly and in-con-VEN-ient. 'truths' can be /truːðz/ or /truːθs/.

text: Only by acknowledging our mistakes can we hope to learn from them.
tip: The k in 'acknowledging' is silent: /əkˈnɒlɪdʒɪŋ/. Stress ON-ly and LEARN.

text: To all intents and purposes, the treaty had become a dead letter.
focus: Idiom: to all intents and purposes
tip: Not 'intensive purposes'! A 'dead letter' is a rule that nobody follows any more.

text: Were the proposal to be rejected, the consequences would be far-reaching.
tip: Stress WERE at the start. 'far-reaching' has two strong beats: FAR-REACH-ing.

text: She has a knack for cutting through the jargon and getting to the heart of the matter.
tip: The k in 'knack' is silent: /næk/. 'jargon' is /ˈdʒɑːɡən/. Stress HEART and MAT-ter.

text: The novelist's prose is so luminous that one almost forgives the meandering plot.
tip: LU-mi-nous /ˈluːmɪnəs/ and me-AN-der-ing /miˈændərɪŋ/.

text: Should you require any further assistance, please do not hesitate to contact us.
tip: 'Should you' replaces 'If you'. HES-i-tate and as-SIS-tance.

text: No sooner had the ink dried on the contract than the dispute flared up again.
tip: Stress NO SOON-er and pause before 'than'. Link 'flared up again' into 'flair-dup-a-gain'.

text: His remarks, however well-intentioned, struck many listeners as patronising.
tip: PAT-ron-is-ing is /ˈpætrənaɪzɪŋ/ in British English. Drop your pitch for 'however well-intentioned'.

text: Far from being a hindrance, her unconventional background proved to be her greatest asset.
tip: HIN-drance has two syllables. un-con-VEN-tion-al, AS-set.

text: The village elders were loath to admit that the prophecy had, in fact, been a hoax.
tip: 'loath' (unwilling) ends in /θ/; 'loathe' (hate) ends in /ð/. PROPH-e-cy is /ˈprɒfəsi/.

text: Little by little, the once-thriving port fell into disrepair, its warehouses left to the mercy of the elements.
tip: Chunks: Little by little | the once-thriving port fell into disrepair | its warehouses left to the mercy of the elements.

q: To what extent should governments regulate artificial intelligence? Hedge your view with 'arguably'.
model: Arguably, some regulation is essential, although too much of it could stifle innovation.
tip: AR-gu-a-bly is stressed on the first syllable. Pause after it.

q: Describe a turning point in your life using an inversion such as 'Only then did I…' or 'Never before had I…'.
keywords: only then|never before|not until|little did|rarely|seldom|no sooner|only when
model: Only then did I realise how much my family had sacrificed for me.
tip: Stress the fronted phrase (ON-ly THEN) and keep the auxiliary 'did' light.

q: 'Exams are the fairest way to assess students.' Concede a point with 'Admittedly' or 'Granted', then disagree.
model: Admittedly, exams are consistent, but they reward memorisation rather than genuine understanding.
tip: Pause after the concession word and stress the contrast that follows.

q: Describe something that went wrong but turned out well. Use the idiom 'a blessing in disguise'.
model: Missing the train was a blessing in disguise, because I met my best friend on the next one.
tip: 'disguise' is /dɪsˈɡaɪz/ with a /z/ at the end. Stress BLESS-ing and dis-GUISE.

q: Explain a tricky idea, such as inflation or gravity, in simple terms. Use 'In other words'.
model: Inflation means prices rise over time. In other words, the same money buys you less.
tip: Pause before and after 'In other words' and stress OTH-er.

text: Only when the last fossil had been catalogued did the young scientists allow themselves a celebration.
tip: Stress ON-ly WHEN and keep 'did' light. CAT-a-logued ends in /ɡd/: /ˈkætəlɒɡd/.

text: The rainforest, teeming with creatures as yet unknown to science, is disappearing at an alarming rate.
tip: Chunks: The rainforest | teeming with creatures as yet unknown to science | is disappearing at an alarming rate.

text: Never before had the observatory's telescope captured such a vivid image of Saturn's rings.
tip: Stress NEV-er be-FORE. ob-SER-va-to-ry is stressed on the second syllable, and 'Saturn's' is /ˈsætənz/.

text: Try as she might, the goalkeeper couldn't quite reach the ball as it curled into the net.
tip: 'Try as she might' means 'however hard she tried'. Pause after it, and link 'curled into' smoothly.

text: The robotics club's latest prototype still struggles to climb the stairs, ingenious though it is.
tip: PRO-to-type and ro-BOT-ics. in-GEN-ious /ɪnˈdʒiːniəs/. Drop your pitch for the last chunk.

text: Be that as it may, the expedition's findings have reshaped our understanding of glaciers.
tip: Pause after 'Be that as it may'. GLA-ci-ers is /ˈɡlæsiəz/ in British English, and ex-pe-DI-tion is stressed on 'DI'.

text: Whereas some insects rely on camouflage, others flaunt their vivid colours as a warning to predators.
tip: To 'flaunt' (show off) is /flɔːnt/; to 'flout' (break a rule) is different. CAM-ou-flage ends in a soft /ʒ/.

text: Such was the excitement in the stadium that the commentator could barely make himself heard.
tip: Stress SUCH and ex-CITE-ment. COM-men-ta-tor is stressed at the start.

text: Not once did the tortoise lose sight of the finishing line, however slowly it plodded along.
tip: Stress NOT ONCE and keep 'did the' quick. 'tortoise' is /ˈtɔːtəs/: the last part sounds like 'tus'.

text: The principal principle of our eco club is refreshingly simple: waste nothing at all.
tip: 'principal' (main) and 'principle' (rule) sound exactly the same: /ˈprɪnsəpl/. Pause at the colon.

q: Should children help design their own school timetable? Give one benefit, then qualify it with 'That said'.
model: Children would feel more responsible for their learning. That said, they might quietly drop every maths lesson!
tip: Pause before and after 'That said', then lighten your voice for the joke at the end.

q: Describe a place in nature that left a lasting impression. Use 'What struck me most was…' or 'What I'll never forget is…'.
keywords: what struck me|what i will never forget
model: What struck me most was the silence of the frozen lake, broken only by the cracking of the ice.
tip: Rise on 'most', pause, then slow down for the picture: SI-lence, FRO-zen LAKE.

q: Explain to a younger child why some animals hibernate. Use 'Put simply'.
model: Put simply, some animals sleep through the winter because there's hardly any food, so they save their energy until spring.
tip: Pause after 'Put simply,'. hi-ber-NATE is stressed at the start: HI-ber-nate.

q: Speculate about life on other planets. Use 'It's conceivable that' or 'There's every chance that'.
model: It's conceivable that tiny microbes live in the ocean beneath the ice on one of Jupiter's moons.
tip: con-CEIV-a-ble is /kənˈsiːvəbl/. Stress TI-ny MI-crobes and JU-pi-ter.

q: Argue that video games can teach useful skills. Use 'Far from being…'.
model: Far from being a waste of time, many games teach teamwork, planning and quick decision-making.
tip: Stress FAR at the start. Give the list an even rhythm: TEAM-work, PLAN-ning, de-CI-sion-mak-ing.

q: Reflect on a mistake that taught you something. Use 'In hindsight'.
model: In hindsight, rushing my science project was a mistake, because the volcano refused to erupt on the day.
tip: HIND-sight is stressed on the first part /ˈhaɪndsaɪt/. Pause after it.

q: Should zoos still exist? Weigh up both sides and finish with 'On balance'.
model: Zoos protect endangered species, though some animals clearly struggle in small enclosures. On balance, good zoos do more good than harm.
tip: Pause before 'On balance', then slow down for your final view. en-DAN-gered, en-CLO-sures.

q: Describe an invention you wish existed. Start with 'If only someone would invent…'.
model: If only someone would invent a backpack that floated behind you, carrying all your heavy books!
tip: Stress ON-ly and let your voice rise with the dream. 'floated' has two syllables.
